rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies a fair-quality blastocyst with loosely grouped ICM and reasonably cohesive TE, and appropriately notes lack of obvious hatching. Minor issue is some uncertainty around expansion stage and possible overinterpretation of zona thinning/collapse from a single image.

Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor diagnosis, endometrial thickness, lifestyle, semen parameters, and first-cycle status with embryo morphology, including the important hydrosalpinx caveat.

Overall logic is clear and internally consistent, with prognosis appropriately balancing embryo grade against favorable patient factors. Small inconsistency arises from discussing implantation versus clinical pregnancy/live birth ranges somewhat loosely.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice: SET at age 34, no routine add-ons, cautious stance on PGT-A, and attention to hydrosalpinx. Minor deviation is some ambiguity around Gardner stage interpretation versus provided lab grade.

Provides practical next steps for current transfer and future planning, including SET, luteal support, hydrosalpinx review, grading clarification, and when to consider PGT-A or sperm DNA fragmentation testing.
